quest.title: Meeting Is Also Parting
quest.description: Acting on intelligence from The Knave, your group arrives at the ruins...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Primogem x30, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So are these the ruins that The Knave was talking about? Whoa, talk about old...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: They seem to be pretty ancient, alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go in and have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Just be careful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place has also been contaminated by Primordial Seawater.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah, and a lot of it, too. A Fontainian would most likely dissolve the moment they fell in.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You should go back to safety, Navia.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, you can't go down if there's Primordial Seawater. It's too dangerous, and it won't be any help for you to just stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, don't get Paimon wrong... We're not saying you're useless! It's just that...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, you're right. I can't do anything in this situation. I'll leave this to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll handle it! Just head back and be careful on the way out.

choices.text: From the look of things here...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That complicates things... Maybe the only way left is forward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, do you want to wait for us here?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: The water levels here are unstable and there's a chance the water will rise... so staying here wouldn't be safe either.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I'll go together with you — perhaps we'll find the exit just up ahead.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Seems like there isn't any other option.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, come with us for now, then. But please, be careful!

dialogues.text: Ahem... Demoiselle.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Demoiselle, what are you doing here by yourself? Would you be standing here till dark if I hadn't come to get you?

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Maybe she just wants some time to herself, Melus.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, was I... Was I sleeping?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Yes, it would appear so.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ugh... I must be tired.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: That's quite possible. However, you were the one that suggested we go out for a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, right... I nearly forgot.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: *yawn* It must have slipped my mind when I dozed off. I haven't had a nap today yet, have I?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (This is a familiar feeling... Yet, something's a little strange.)

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Is something the matter, Demoiselle?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, no... No, I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I was just trying to recall why we came out for a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Do you remember Mr. Giverny? He'd requested our help before with foreign merchants who had a debt dispute with him, and we'd resolved the matter not long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: We were headed to see how things were going with him at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah, right. Yes, I remember now.

dialogues.speaker: Giverny
dialogues.text: Oh? Miss Navia! Ah, and Mr. Melus and Mr. Silver too, haha! It's good to see all of you.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Giverny
dialogues.text: I've been great. Thanks to your help, those bothersome merchants finally realized that I wasn't the one they were looking for — why, I wasn't even the guarantor for that person!

dialogues.speaker: Giverny
dialogues.text: They were knocking at my door day and night... Even my neighbor, Aubenas, was getting fed up with them!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Sometimes, force is required to calm someone down and get them to listen to what you have to say.

dialogues.speaker: Giverny
dialogues.text: Haha, that's right. Oh, by the way, Bernette... What was it that you wanted to give to Miss Navia, again?

dialogues.speaker: Bernette
dialogues.text: Oh, yes. One moment, I have it right here.

dialogues.speaker: Bernette
dialogues.text: Miss Navia, these are some flower seeds that I prepared. Please, take them. They're a very good variety, and they'll become very big and beautiful once they bloom.

dialogues.speaker: Bernette
dialogues.text: I don't know what we would have done without your help, so this is a little token of our appreciation. I hope you won't refuse!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Did you cultivate them yourself? Thank you so much — I'll certainly take them. Melus, we do still have some empty flower pots at home, right?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Why, we can have as many pots as you'd like, Demoiselle.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Perfect — in that case, we'll swap out some of the decorative plants for some of Mrs. Bernette's flowers...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Very well.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (Wait, something seems to be off here...)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Excuse me, Madam. If I'm not mistaken, your name is Bernette, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Bernette
dialogues.text: That's right. Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, it's nothing. This is the first time we've ever met, but your name seemed familiar to me. I must have heard it when I was discussing things with your husband previously.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (I've heard this name before... sometime recently. I'm sure of it...)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (And why are there so few people around here? Where did everyone go?)

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: We must mind the time, Demoiselle. We still have important things to attend to today.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm? We do? Like what?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Well, now, did you forget?

dialogues.speaker: Melissa
dialogues.text: Miss Navia! Here you are! I've been looking for you... Please come to the opera house — your trial is about to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: My trial? Wait... Wh—Why would I need to go to the opera house?

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Yes, she's right, Demoiselle. It's just about time now, so we should get going.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh? Alright then...

dialogues.speaker: Essonnes
dialogues.text: Look, it's Navia! She's here!

dialogues.speaker: Jolienne
dialogues.text: And her two attendants are with her. Goodness, everyone's finally here!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (There sure are a lot of people here to see the trial, and they all seem to be oddly... excited about something. I even know some of these people.)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (Korina, Desyree, Joinville, Jolienne, Essonnes... Why are so many people here? And why do I have no recollection of this case?)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (And as for the judge... Huh? Where's Monsieur Neuvillette?)

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Please sit in the defendant's seat. Don't worry, Silver and I shall accompany you.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Alright... But are you sure you can stand behind me?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Typically, it wouldn't be allowed, but today is an exception.

dialogues.speaker: All
dialogues.text: Hey, what kind of place do they think this is... C'mon, do they have any idea what they're doing!? Seriously...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Enough with the whispering! Could someone please tell me where Monsieur Neuvillette is, and why I'm standing trial?

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: My dear Miss Navia, have you not yet realized what you've done? In that case, allow me to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: As all here know, you are Master Callas's successor, the head of the Spina di Rosula — someone held in high regard by every soul in Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: After you took over the Spina, you treated all of us just like the late Master Callas had. If anyone in need reached out to you for help, you responded.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Not only you, but your butler, your subordinates... Nearly everyone in the Spina di Rosula fought for the well-being of those in Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Wait a moment. Aren't you just proving that I'm a good person?

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Yes, correct, absolutely right! And that is why you stand accused! You have helped so many people get through so many difficulties — you are one with us... we are inseparable.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: We are one big family, all of us who are from Poisson, inextricably linked — and with you being so important... We couldn't possibly do without you.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Therefore, this fair and honorable court shall declare you guilty, and you shall stay here. You will be together with us — forever.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? What are you saying...?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah... Everything you have said is correct. I have indeed done a lot for my hometown, and I would be willing to be with you all... But what is the purpose of having me stand here like this? What is there to discuss?

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Oh... Well, if that's what you think, then I have no further comments.

dialogues.speaker: Jolienne
dialogues.text: How wonderful, Miss Navia.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (I know all these people... Why are they laughing?)

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Huh. I seem to remember now... Yes, I get it. This trial is...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Wait just a moment... This isn't right!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Melus?

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: What was that, Mr. Melus? Our conclusion is very clear and unanimous. Let the court judge her now! She's guilty!

dialogues.speaker: Desyree
dialogues.text: Stay here, Navia! You're one of us!

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Demoiselle, don't admit guilt. This trial means to keep you here forever.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: I wish to exercise my right to defend our lady. Mr. Joinville, you only know of Navia's goodness, but nothing of her utterly independent mind.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: She was born a free and independent spirit. She has never been tied down by anything — indeed, even the death of Master Callas couldn't stop her.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Her actions cannot serve as proof that she identifies herself as part of any group. She merely acted as an individual, extending her hand to help others.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Please do not mistake her actions as being otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Really? As an individual, you say? Don't forget, we are all Fontainians here... This is the Nation of Justice, the Nation of Hydro.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Even if Miss Navia only voluntarily rendered her assistance, that doesn't change the fact that her beautiful soul must return to everyone. Water accepts all, blends with all... It will surely accept her kindness.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Everything is measured here in the Nation of Hydro. And in the end, everyone shall meld together. Thus, when a unanimous opinion emerges, that opinion represents justice.

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Now, I speak for everyone. "Our" opinion is consistent — Navia should stay. "We" and Navia are one!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: And you would call this justice? Preposterous. You are merely jealous that Demoiselle still has a chance to exist as an individual!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Have you forgotten how much you all once longed to become individuals... to become independent?

dialogues.speaker: All
dialogues.text: Do you mean to defy our justice?

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: If your justice is flawed, then why should we acknowledge it?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: As you said, we can also have our own justice. Silver and I shall defend Demoiselle.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: And that is how we will enforce justice.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (Ugh, my head... it hurts...)

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Demoiselle.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Silver, it hurts... My head is spinning... All I can see is stars swirling in front of me.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (I remember now... everything that seemed odd from the very beginning...)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (Korina, Desyree, Joinville, Jolienne, Essonnes... And Mr. Giverny and Mrs. Bernette, who we met earlier...)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (Even Melus and Silver... I don't want to admit it, but... But they're all dead!)

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Don't be afraid, and don't admit guilt. We will protect you to the very end.

dialogues.speaker: Desyree
dialogues.text: Absurd! Who are you to say that she cannot be judged!? We are the majority, and in the Nation of Trials, the majority is absolute justice. We are the will of all!

dialogues.speaker: Jolienne
dialogues.text: Don't let them escape! We shall keep Navia here with us!

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: Mr. Melus and Mr. Silver... Must you be so stubborn?

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: How could the two of you possibly hope to stand against the collective? Do not resist — this judgment is fair and just... Navia belongs to "us."

dialogues.speaker: Joinville
dialogues.text: After all that happened, she should not be left alone in Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What are you saying!?

dialogues.speaker: Desyree
dialogues.text: No more excuses!

dialogues.speaker: Essonnes
dialogues.text: He says we're jealous... Jealous, hah! How could she possibly be an independent individual?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What's with these people...

dialogues.speaker: All
dialogues.text: Who's jealous of her? She belongs to us! Miss... Navia... She...
Silence!

dialogues.speaker: Jolienne
dialogues.text: Huh! That's...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Monsieur Neuvillette!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Such commotion is prohibited in the court. The accusations you just presented are nonsense, and cannot constitute a proper trial.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The court will adjourn for the rest of the day — in this, I shall hear no objections from any unauthorized party.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Our thanks, Monsieur Neuvillette.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please leave with me, Miss Navia, while there is still time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Go on now, Demoiselle. This is your only chance to leave this place. What, can't bear to leave us behind or something?

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Melus!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Haha, my apologies. I couldn't resist making one little joke once I realized that this shall be our last goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Melus... Silver...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Quickly, you must come now!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Goodbye, Demoiselle.

dialogues.speaker: Silver
dialogues.text: Farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, wait! Just a second!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Navia!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: You're awake. Good.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I must have been dreaming... Melus and Silver were still alive, and they were... they were defending me at some insane trial.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It looks like you're alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did all the sad feelings cause you to have a nightmare? Paimon... could give you a hug...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The ruins you were exploring suffered a cave-in. When I arrived, I found you falling toward the water.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: You were just about to be dissolved within, but I... Hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm? ...What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...I think I saw two Oceanids protecting you. It was only for a moment, perhaps even a fraction of a second, but they gave me the chance to retrieve you.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Were it not for their intervention, I would not have been able to rescue you before your consciousness dissipated.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, did you say Oceanids? You mean like what happened with Vacher?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So people that are dissolved became Oceanids?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Perhaps those two Oceanids were the people you saw in your dream.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I always told them that they didn't have to protect me... To think that they'd keep doing so even after death...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, please come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neuvillette, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, I am quite alright. Perhaps there's something we could chat about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why do you look so stiff all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon knows! You're the type who feels awkward when there's nothing to talk about, right?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I merely thought that we should give Navia some time to herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why didn't you just say so, then? Don't you think it's even more awkward to call us over like this and then have nothing to talk about?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hmm, I suppose so...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: By the way, Sigewinne sends her regards.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Ah, Sigewinne. I hope all is well with her these days. Her work in the Fortress of Meropide has not been too much for her, has it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way, don't worry. She's doing fine down there. She's an amazing head nurse!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I see. Well, that is good. I have always worried that Sigewinne would need a lot of time to understand the world of humanity, just as I have.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and the Duke also says hi, even though Sigewinne made him do that... He hopes that you haven't been overwhelmed by all that's happened lately.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Thank you. I have indeed been busy lately, and I also hope that everything is going well in the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh. He still doesn't know what to talk about... Let's chat about something else, then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're the expert here, Paimon, what should we talk about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Neuvillette... Uh, you're probably quite the swimmer, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hmm? Yes, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this isn't going anywhere... Let's try something else! How did you find these ruins? Did The Knave tell you?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Yes, in fact. I had arranged to meet you in Poisson, but when I arrived, I discovered that the Fatui were helping the residents evacuate. They had even transported a large quantity of supplies to the area.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Amid my astonishment, I ran into The Knave, and we had a chat. She informed me that she had asked you to investigate the ancient ruins here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. We originally planned to meet up with you, but we thought you might still be busy with all those official documents. We didn't think exploring the ruins would take very long, and who would've thought you'd wrap things up so quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I hope Navia can get back on her feet.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we've reached the end...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: This is the place. There should not be any other hidden spaces in the vicinity.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The path sure had some twists and turns, but it turns out that this place isn't actually that big.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There seems to be something on the wall.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Stone slates? It seems like they were put here as an offering... Could we take them down and have a look?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Perhaps we should just leave them be for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, there are four locations in total, but only three stone slates. The slate that should be in the first empty spot is missing.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The surrounding walls also show signs of damage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's something written below, let Paimon see... "Reason dictates that this nation be destroyed. I shall record the history of its future here in its past..." Uh, say what?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It feels like someone left these slates and these words here for a purpose. But does he mean that Fontaine should be destroyed?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: That would fit the circumstances dictated by the prophecy, yes. Indeed, the slates' contents correspond to it. Take the second slate, for example.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a person kneeling here. She seems so... dedicated, and there's a whole bunch of other people behind her doing the same. She's facing this... What is this? Some kinda island in the sky?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And is that... Lady Furina in the third image? Did the Hydro Archon fall into the water?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And is that a ring of people around her? Paimon doesn't quite get it... are they all in the water?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The fourth image... I know this one. This exactly matches the content of the prophecy...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The people will all be dissolved into the waters, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, they do seem to match...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: More information should be hidden in these slates, but I fear I cannot easily uncover it — most likely due to us missing the first slate. I am very sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Don't blame yourself, Monsieur Neuvillette. Deciphering ancient stone slates isn't one of your duties.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon's getting the chills just looking at these slates...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This says that it's "the history of the future," right? That means the prophecy's sure to come true...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...I really hope it doesn't mean that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, Paimon feels like these images are kinda weird when you look at them together...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm...

choices.text: I get what you mean, Paimon.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's right! If the images are in chronological order, shouldn't the fourth — the waters drowning Fontaine — come before the third, where the Hydro Archon herself falls into the water?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: And yet the order is reversed here.

choices.text: The second image is also quite concerning.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If we go by timing, Lady Furina only emerges in the third image... That means that the person in the second image might be the previous Hydro Archon.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Egeria, then... I had never met her, but her appearance here does match the records.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: The previous Archon kneeling before the floating island in the skies, as if confessing a sin...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Did she herself commit that sin? And if not, why would she be in such a posture...?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Also, I'm still wondering why these ancient stone slates are here at all. Judging from their contents... Could this place be the origin of the prophecy? Does that mean that someone, or some people, once saw these slates?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But who would have created these slates and left these words here?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: It seems that any further clues will have to come from Furina.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: In that case, there's no time to lose. There's nothing else to be gained here, so let's head back first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. We'd better just get somewhere safe for now...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Honestly, who created the slates doesn't matter now. The real question is whether things will truly play out as the prophecy foretells or not.)

choices.text: What sin are the people in the images confessing to?
The issue is the order of the third and fourth images, right?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Let's split up here. I'm going to check on what's happening with the Spina — you know how it is. There's some things you just need to be there for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You still have the energy for that, Navia? Paimon's already beat...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Just head back to the Fleuve Cendre and have a rest, then. Thanks for keeping me company all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I'll depart as well. Thanks for your hard work today. Rest well, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, I will go talk to Furina tomorrow morning to ask about the stone slates.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I'm sure that you're concerned about this matter as well. If you have time, drop by my office. I will share the results of our discussion with you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright. See you tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you really gonna talk to her about this directly? Will that be a problem...? Ugh, Paimon's getting a little scared now that it's come to this.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: She has long been harboring secrets, and will not give them up easily — which makes it all the more my duty to ensure that she understands the present situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we'll leave it in your hands, then — you're probably the best person to talk to her, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I will be carefully considering my words tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, our safe house at the Fleuve Cendre is always open to you, as ever. So please don't think you're an imposition.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll be on my way, then!
